problem: The install log lives only in memory (last `LOG_KEEP` lines); a failed real run leaves no evidence to send the developer.
fix: write every page line, the computer's addresses and routes to pisophone-setup-log-<stamp>.txt (0600, passwords masked); link it from the error banner and the last page

problem: *Try again* on the Install step after the router password was set logs in with an empty password (the session's `Ssh` was set to `""`); every retry fails the same way. Only *Back* to the Router step reloads the saved password.
fix: before the install re-probe the router; with a password use the saved one (use_saved_password), else send the owner to the Router step

test.where: router/tests/test_setup_web.py (SU-09 checks, a core whose router gets a password after run 1)

problem: A refused ssh login is reported as "the connection to the router was lost ... Try again", which sends the owner round in a loop.
fix: tell a refused ssh login (exit 255, Permission denied) from a lost connection and say which password is needed

problem: PLDT and Converge modems are at 192.168.1.1, like a factory router. The README tells the owner to keep the computer's Wi-Fi on the shop network for the phone, so the computer has two 192.168.1.x networks and may reach the modem: "No router found" or "not an OpenWrt router".
fix: detect two interfaces in the router's range (or the router address reached through Wi-Fi) and stop with advice; README recommends the owner's phone hotspot (D2)

test.where: router/tests/test_pisophone_setup.py (SU-01 checks, fake address tables for Windows, Linux, macOS); RS56 (a)

problem: With the router cable in, the computer usually sends its internet through the router (a cable has a better route metric than Wi-Fi), and the factory router has none (WAN unplugged, or WAN 192.168.1.x clashes with its own LAN). The coin box software and the offline bundle then fail to download: the setup without the router's internet (feature 011) breaks exactly where it is meant to help.
fix: download coin box software (every chip), installer files and app.json at Start; before the router packages check the website answers, else ask to unplug the router cable for the download (D5)

problem: Only 10.0.0.1 and 192.168.1.1 are tried. OpenWrt-based vendor firmware uses other factory addresses (GL.iNet 192.168.8.1, Cudy 192.168.10.1): the page searches for ever.
fix: also probe the gateway named by the cable's DHCP lease with the OpenWrt check, and name the address found

problem: An apk router (OpenWrt 25.x) is offered the online way after the offline way refuses; the router then fails at `opkg update` with "no internet or DNS?".
fix: refuse an apk router (or one without opkg) before any change, naming its release and the supported ones (D1)

problem: A rental phone downloads the app from the website over PisoKiosk, so it needs the router's internet. After a setup without the router's internet the Phones step still shows the QR code; the phone then stops at Android's generic "Can't set up device".
fix: before the Phones step shows the QR code, the router must reach the app's address in app.json; else say plug the modem into WAN and re-check

problem: The coin box software list and image are fetched without the program's `User-Agent` (used everywhere else because Python's own is sometimes refused).
fix: send USER_AGENT on the manifest and image requests

problem: `--install-service` starts the file from where it was downloaded (often `~/Downloads`); moved or deleted, the setup page no longer starts at boot.
fix: --install-service copies the program to /var/lib/pisophone-setup and starts that copy

problem: On Windows 10 the built-in OpenSSH is 8.1, older than `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE` (8.4): logins that need a password (a re-run, the coin test, Telegram) may hang or fail.
fix: decide after RS56 (b) on Windows 10 (OpenSSH 8.1 has no SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE): if logins with a password fail, say so on the first page with the fix

problem: After the move to 10.0.0.1 only Windows asks for a new address by itself (`ipconfig /renew`). Linux, macOS and the headless Armbian box keep their 192.168.1.x address until someone replugs the cable; after 4 minutes the setup stops.
fix: after network restart switch every LAN port off for 3 s and on (DSA: ip link; swconfig: the switch command) so every computer asks for a new address (D3)

test.where: router/tests/test_install.py (SU-03 checks, fake ip and swconfig); RS57 (a)

problem: Pairing takes the first station that joins `PisoCoinBox` with the public default password. With two freshly written boxes switched on at the bench (*Set up the next unit*), a router can pair the other unit's box and trust it with its gateway key.
fix: program reads mac= from PISO-HELLO after writing (the Wi-Fi station MAC, esp32_firmware/src/main.cpp:228-235) and sends BOX_EXPECT_MAC; pair_box admits only that MAC; empty = any box as today (D4)

test.where: router/tests/test_setup.py (SU-11 checks: a wrong MAC joins first); router/tests/test_setup_web.py; RS57 (b)

problem: The router side has the same apk gap for a setup by hand (`wget ... install.sh | sh`).
fix: install.sh and preflight stop with a clear message when opkg is missing, before any download or move

problem: The modem-range checks compare only the first three numbers of the address with 10.0.0 or 10.0.30, ignore the netmask (a 10.x.x.x/8 lease clashes too) and run only when the WAN is up at that moment: after a setup without the router's internet a modem plugged in later can clash in silence.
fix: compare WAN and LAN/guest ranges with the netmask; status and the monitor re-check once the WAN is up and alert

problem: A router whose release feeds no longer answer (an old release moved to the archive, a vendor build) fails at `opkg update` with "no internet or DNS?" although it has internet.
fix: when opkg update fails but the ping works, say the release's package sources do not answer, name the release, point to docs/ROUTERS.md

problem: `restart_router_access` restarts dropbear and uhttpd **before** the `DONE` state is written and the summary is sent. If the restart ends the setup's own ssh session, the setup stops half way and the computer gets no summary.
fix: write the state and send the results first, then restart dropbear and uhttpd in the background; or wont-fix with RS57 (c) evidence

test.where: router/tests/test_setup.py (SU-08 checks, a restart that hangs up the session); RS57 (c)

problem: PisoPhone only: a mistyped shop Wi-Fi password is saved, the box never joins, and a new run gets `already-set-up`; the only way out is writing the software again with an erase and typing ERASE. The box also does not say why it cannot join.
fix: until the box has joined a Wi-Fi once and has no payment, take new Wi-Fi details over USB (setup=joining, why=); the program offers Change the Wi-Fi details (D6)

test.where: esp32_firmware/host_tests (SU-16: joined once or a payment -> already-set-up); router/tests/test_phone_only.py; RS58
